Retro Home-On-Wheels: A Beautiful 1972 Boles Aero

CA
By Chloe Adams Car Culture & Restomod Editor • via Silodrome Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Silodrome Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • This is a refurbished Boles Aero XL travel trailer from 1972, with a gleaming aluminum shell and an interior fit-out that’s period correct for the era in which it was made.
  • Inside you’ll find everything you need from a home-on-wheels, including sleeping space for up to four, a bathroom with a toilet and shower, a fully-equipped kitchenette, and a dinette with seating space for four.

⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • CHLOE ADAMS Car Culture & Restomod Editor

Heritage Preservation vs Modern Performance

Automotive passion is increasingly defined by the synthesis of analog soul and contemporary engineering. This coverage from Silodrome illustrates how bespoke builders, private collectors, and restomod artists are preserving the golden eras of internal combustion while adopting carbon fiber composites and precision craftsmanship.

Big Picture: Auction hammer prices and enthusiast demand indicate sustained historical appreciation for rare, analog driver's vehicles.

This is a refurbished Boles Aero XL travel trailer from 1972, with a gleaming aluminum shell and an interior fit-out that’s period correct for the era in which it was made.

📌 The Core Development

Inside you’ll find everything you need from a home-on-wheels, including sleeping space for up to four, a bathroom with a toilet and shower, a fully-equipped kitchenette, and a dinette with seating space for four.

Boles Manufacturing was founded in Burbank, California, in 1946 – the company built a popular line of aluminum travel trailers for 34 years, and it had all started out with a single trailer built in a one-car garage. The Boles Aero never reached Airstream’s national popularity , but their polished aluminum trailers developed a cult following all their own.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Boles Manufacturing was founded in Burbank, California, in 1946 – the company built a popular line of aluminum travel trailers for 34 years, and it had all started out with a single trailer built in a one-car garage. Image courtesy of Boles Aero.

The company was founded by Don and Jeanette Boles, and their built their trailers using methods Don had learned making aircraft.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

In 1939, Don Boles was one of the first 37 candidates picked for a new four-year tool and die apprenticeship. The US Department of Labor had set it up as part of the Roosevelt administration’s plan to pull the country out of the Great Depression. It was an interesting time in world history, WWII kicked off that same year across the Atlantic, and two years later the United States would join the conflict after the attack on Pearl Harbor.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Boles served it at Lockheed’s aircraft plant in Burbank, learning aircraft design and construction methods, and he went on to win several awards for tools he designed to improve the way aluminum parts were made. He graduated as a journeyman tool and die maker in 1943, right in the midst of WWII when men with his skillset were in huge demand.

After a short assignment with General Electric in Cleveland, Ohio, Boles enlisted in the U.S. Navy and was posted to a base at Norman, Oklahoma. No housing could be found there for his wife, Jeanette, and their three children, so he bought a used 27 foot trailer, and the family lived in it for the rest of his military service. The couple had met at Burbank High School and married a month after she graduated, when she was 16 and he was 18.
